subject: Order Form redlines — termination/auto-renew options
messages:
From: Jessica Su <jessica.su@acme.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-02-12T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form redlines — Term & Auto-Renew

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We ran the proposed Order Form past legal and procurement and have attached redlines (see acme_redlines_20260212.docx). High-level asks:

- We'd like to limit Redwood's termination-for-convenience exposure. Our legal team is asking for mutual termination for convenience with 30 days' notice and a pro-rata refund for pre-paid fees.
- Auto-renew: prefer 12-month renewal but want a 30-day opt-out window rather than 60.
- If Redwood insists on longer notice or non-refundable pre-paid commits, we need clear transition assistance and data export guarantees.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether you can accept the 30-day opt-out / pro-rata refund? If not, what alternatives do you suggest?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like to close by the end of this month.

Thanks,
Jessica
Jessica Su
Lead, Procurement
Acme Corp
Attachment: acme_redlines_20260212.docx (document with tracked changes)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Su <jessica.su@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-13T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — Term & Auto-Renew

Hi Jessica — thanks for sending this over and for the deadline heads-up. I pulled in our legal and commercial leads to assess. Preliminary notes:

- We understand Acme's ask for a 30-day mutual termination with pro-rata refund, but that materially increases revenue risk for Redwood on committed capacity.
- Two paths to consider (we can offer either):
  1) Mutual termination for convenience with 60 days' notice + capped buyout (e.g., 3 months of committed fees) + transition assistance (30 days support)
  2) Keep 12-month auto-renew but agree to a 60-day opt-out window (not 30) and provide data export / transition support; no refunds for usage, pro-rata credits only for pre-paid committed fees.

Rishi — can you confirm whether legal is comfortable with language along the lines of the first option (mutual TFC with capped buyout)?
Karthik — need your view on commercial impact and whether we can accept a 60-day opt-out for a deal this size; if we concede further, what pricing guardrails should we require?

Jessica — if either option is acceptable to Acme, we can provide specific redline text and an updated Order Form.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Attachment: referenced acme_redlines_20260212.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-14T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — Term & Auto-Renew

Grace — legal here. We can accept a mutual termination-for-convenience clause, but it should include a cap to limit exposure. Suggested approach: 60 days' written notice and a termination fee equal to the greater of (i) three months' average monthly committed fees or (ii) unbilled, prepaid amounts for the remainder of the commitment. This preserves predictability for finance and protects against mid-term churn that leaves capacity unused.

Suggested clause (draft):
"Either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. In the event of termination for convenience by either party, Customer shall pay to Redwood an early termination fee equal to the greater of (a) three (3) months of Customer's average monthly committed fees under this Order Form or (b) any unbilled, prepaid amounts for the remainder of the then-current committed term. Redwood will provide reasonable transition assistance for thirty (30) days following termination at no additional charge."

We should avoid a 30-day window or an unconditional pro-rata refund. If Acme insists on 30 days, we can consider it for pilot or limited accounts only and require higher termination fees.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-15T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — Term & Auto-Renew

Grace — commercial perspective: ACME is a strategic mid-market expansion opportunity (deal ACME-4589). I'm OK with the 60-day + 3mo cap approach, but recommend we also: 

- Require a minimum monthly commitment for the first 90 days after signature (to avoid immediate churn).
- Limit the 30-day transition assistance to operational handover only (we'll not absorb bespoke migration work).
- Keep the auto-renew at 12 months but agree to a 60-day opt-out (not 30). If Acme pushes for 30 days, counter with 30 days only for pilot accounts or if they accept a one-time onboarding fee equal to one month's committed spend.

I'll update the commercial language and pricing variables if you want me to draft the exact redline. Also noted: HubSpot deal link below for reference.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/deal/ACME-4589

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Su <jessica.su@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-16T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Final — Order Form updates on Termination & Auto-Renew

Hi Jessica — thanks for your patience while we reviewed. After discussing internally, Redwood can agree to the following compromise:

1) Mutual termination for convenience with sixty (60) days' prior written notice.
2) Termination fee cap: the greater of (a) three (3) months of Customer's average monthly committed fees under the Order Form or (b) any unbilled, prepaid amounts for the remainder of the then-current committed term.
3) Redwood will provide reasonable transition assistance for thirty (30) days post-termination limited to standard operational handover (data export, access handoff, runbook). Bespoke migration work or engineering integrations will be scoped and billed separately.
4) Auto-renew remains on a 12-month cadence; Acme will have a 60-day opt-out window prior to renewal.

I've attached the updated redline (redline_orderform_20260216.docx) that implements the clause above. If that looks good, I can route the updated Order Form for signature via DocuSign.

DocuSign (pre-fill): https://docusign.example/embedded/tx-12345
Drive (updated redline): https://drive.example/redwood/acme/orderform-redline-20260216

Next steps: please confirm Acme's acceptance of the above language and we'll issue the DocuSign packet. If you want to keep pushing for 30 days + pro-rata refund, let us know but we will need to add either (a) a higher termination fee or (b) a one-time onboarding fee to offset risk.

Best regards,
Grace
